version.changelog: After you update, run twelvetake-reaper-mcp --install-bridge. If REAPER is running the 1.7.8 bridge or later, you don't have to do anything in REAPER. If you installed with ReaPack, synchronize your packages instead. Fixed: - add_envelope_point refused on a track that didn't have that envelope yet. It asked you to create the envelope in REAPER first. It now creates a missing Volume, Pan, Width, Mute or Trim Volume envelope, or a Pre-FX one, the way REAPER does when you show it: the new envelope starts with a point at 0:00 holding the track's current value. Your track selection stays as it was. *(Found while answering a follow-up from @gitickle in issue #20.)* - render_project erased the project's render start delay. Every render through the tool reset the delay to 0 seconds, and rendered without the project's options to embed metadata, stretch markers and take markers or to render in two passes. The tool now uses those options and leaves the delay as you set it. It still renders without the delay, because REAPER's countdown window would stop the bridge until someone closed it. - The server reported the wrong version to your AI client. 1.8.0 and 1.9.0 said they were version 1.30.0, the version of the MCP library they're built on. The server now reports its own version. Added: - render_project tells you what the project's render settings did to the file. A render uses the project's own normalization, limiter, fades, silence trimming and padding. The response now lists the ones that applied in processing, for example a -11 LUFS normalization target or a 3.5 s fade-out. Pass skip_postprocessing to render without them, for a file you want to measure or compare. The tool's description used to say that only the file format came from the project.
